object.value: Ontology for Digital Markers in Mental Health (ODIM-MH)
Ontology for organizing measurements, features, context, provenance, and digital phenotypes for wearable/device-based health studies.
A process or activity that computes features or infers phenotypes.
A collection of data items associated with a participant or study process.
A feature computed from raw measurements and possibly other features.
Layer for features derived from measurements.
A hardware or software platform used to collect data.
Higher-level construct inferred from features and measurements.
The distance travelled or otherwise attributed to an activity observation.
Energy expended during a stated observation interval or activity.
The duration attributed to an exercise activity.
An attribute computed from one or more measurements.
The number of flights of stairs climbed during a stated observation interval.
The rate at which the heart beats, observed by a heart-rate measurement.
Variation in the time intervals between successive heart beats, without specifying the calculation method.
Heart-rate variability expressed as the root mean square of successive beat-interval differences.
Heart-rate variability expressed as the standard deviation of normal-to-normal beat intervals.
Software interface used to capture or transfer data.
A single observation or data point recorded by a device or system.
A single observation recorded by a device or system, optionally linked to a QUDT QuantityValue and SOSA properties.
Layer for raw observations/measurements captured from devices and apps.
A meta-class grouping the modeling layers in this ontology.
An individual taking part in a study.
The rate of respiratory cycles observed over a unit of time.
An activity/process that captures sensor data and produces measurements.
The classified stage of sleep observed for a stated interval.
The number of steps attributed to a stated observation interval or temporal grain.

A heart-rate quantity designated by its producing system as resting heart rate. The designation does not entail a directly observed resting context, a shared derivation algorithm, or equivalence between different vendors' estimates.

A source record containing a value that its producing system designates as a resting heart-rate estimate. This class does not entail direct observation during a known resting state or a disclosed derivation method.
Associates an activity/computation with a device agent.
Indicates a measurement used in computing a feature.
DL-safe annotation linking ontology terms to SKOS concepts.
Links an entity to an agent it is attributed to (e.g., a dataset to a participant).
Associates a dataset with the participant it was collected from.
Links an entity (e.g., measurement/feature/dataset) to the computation/activity that generated it.
